source: NCERT Class XII, Themes in Indian History Part III, Ch. 13 (Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement).

sections.heading: 1. Gandhi's Early Years and Methods
points: **Mahatma Gandhi** returned to India from **South Africa in 1915**, where he had developed **Satyagraha (truth-force / non-violent resistance)**.
His mentor was **Gopal Krishna Gokhale**; his early Indian satyagrahas: **Champaran (1917, indigo), Ahmedabad mill strike (1918), Kheda (1918)**.
Gandhi's philosophy: **truth (satya), non-violence (ahimsa), self-reliance (swadeshi, khadi)**.

sections.heading: 2. The Great Movements
points: **Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–22)** — boycott of British institutions; called off after **Chauri Chaura (1922)**.
**Civil Disobedience Movement (1930)** — began with the **Dandi Salt March (1930)** — breaking the salt law; wide participation.
**Round Table Conferences** (London); the **Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931)**; **Poona Pact (1932)** with Ambedkar on separate electorates.
**Quit India Movement (1942)** — 'Do or Die'; demand for immediate independence; mass upsurge, harsh repression.

sections.heading: 3. Gandhi and the Masses
points: Gandhi transformed the national movement into a **mass movement** — reaching peasants, workers, women and the poor.
He worked for **Hindu-Muslim unity**, against **untouchability (called untouchables 'Harijans')**, and for village self-reliance.
He used simple symbols (khadi, charkha/spinning wheel, dhoti) that connected with ordinary Indians.

sections.heading: 4. Sources and Last Days
points: The chapter uses sources like **newspapers, private letters, and autobiographies** to study Gandhi.
Gandhi opposed the **Partition** and worked for communal harmony; he was **assassinated on 30 January 1948** (by Nathuram Godse).
His methods (satyagraha, non-violence) inspired movements worldwide.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Gandhi returned from South Africa in 1915; early satyagrahas: Champaran (1917), Ahmedabad, Kheda (1918).
Non-Cooperation (1920–22, ended after Chauri Chaura); Civil Disobedience (1930, Dandi Salt March).
Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931); Poona Pact (1932, with Ambedkar).
Quit India Movement (1942) = 'Do or Die'.
Gandhi assassinated on 30 January 1948.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: Gandhi returned to India from **South Africa in 1915**.
**Champaran (1917)** was his **first satyagraha in India** (indigo peasants).
The **Civil Disobedience Movement began with the Dandi Salt March (1930)**.
**Quit India (1942)** gave the slogan **'Do or Die'**.
